[[User:Kevstuff|Kevstuff]] ([[User talk:Kevstuff|talk]]) 21:11, 21 October 2026 (UTC) == External link suggestion (conflict of interest disclosed) == {{request edit}} Disclosure: I built the tools below, so I am not adding anything to the article myself and will leave the decision to other editors. Readers of this article will mostly want to know whether their own site or server is affected. Two free resources may be useful in an "External links" section, if editors think they meet [[WP:EL]]: * An open-source (MIT) script that lists every PHP installation on a server and flags PHP-FPM processes still running a replaced binary after the update: https://github.com/KyleClouthier/php2shell-check * A browser check that reads a site's public signals (headers, CMS fingerprints) and explains what to ask the host if the version is hidden: https://simgen.dev/php-patch-check . This one is on my own business site, which also offers paid help, so editors may prefer the GitHub link alone. Happy for either or neither to be used. Thanks for maintaining the article. [[User:Simgen321|Simgen321]] ([[User talk:Simgen321|talk]]) 21:54, 21 October 2026 (UTC) == Suggested source for detection and response (COI disclosure) == {{Edit COI}} I'm the author of the post below, so I'm disclosing a conflict of interest and not adding it myself. I briefly added it earlier on the wrong sentence and have removed it. The article doesn't yet cover how organizations can check whether they were compromised before patching. My post covers this (preserving logs, reviewing activity from 20 October onward, signs of web shells, and rotating secrets because one bug can leak server memory). Editors may find it useful for a "Detection and response" section, or may prefer a vendor source such as Huntress or watchTowr for the same points. {{cite web |last=Nagar |first=Gourav |date=21 October 2026 |title=PHP2Shell: AI Didn't Find the Bug. It Made the Bug Cheap. |url=https://www.thedigitalforensics.com/infosec/php2shell-ai-didnt-find-the-bug-it-made-the-bug-cheap |website=The DFIR Blog |access-date=21 October 2026}} [[Special:Contributions/~2026-56359-71|~2026-56359-71]] ([[User talk:~2026-56359-71|talk]]) 23:16, 21 October 2026 (UTC) [[Special:Contributions/~2026-56359-71|~2026-56359-71]] ([[User talk:~2026-56359-71|talk]]) 23:16, 21 October 2026 (UTC) :Proposed addition to Impact: “Security researchers advised organizations to preserve logs, review activity from 20 October onward, and rotate credentials, since one of the flaws could leak server memory without code execution.” [[User:AceZ1q|AceZ1q]] ([[User talk:AceZ1q|talk]]) 23:46, 21 October 2026 (UTC)
